title: Chicken or Turkey Salad with Italian Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey salad with Italian dressing is a ready‑to‑eat dish made from boiled or roasted poultry, fresh vegetables (lettuce, tomato, cucumber, pepper) and a flavorful dressing based on olive oil, vinegar, herbs and spices. It is convenient for quick meals and works well as a light lunch or dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Italian dressing often includes oregano, basil and garlic, giving the salad a Mediterranean aroma.
Chicken and turkey are lean sources of high‑quality protein that are easily digested.
Poultry salads are popular in diet plans because they are low in calories and high in protein.
Traditionally served cold, the salad can also be gently warmed if a warm dish is preferred.
Some regions add Parmesan cheese or olives for extra flavor.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Lean poultry contains little saturated fat, making the salad suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Poultry is abundant in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidants in the dressing
items.content: Olive oil and herbs in Italian dressing supply polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Fresh vegetables add dietary fiber, beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chicken or turkey, experiencing skin reactions or digestive issues.

items.title: Sodium content in dressing
items.content: Prepared Italian dressings often contain salt; people monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt versions.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: If the meat is not properly cooked or stored, there is a risk of salmonella or Campylobacter infection.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Some ready‑made dressings may contain preservatives and artificial flavors that not everyone tolerates well.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The salad is ready to eat straight from the package. It can be enjoyed on its own, wrapped in a flatbread, used as a sandwich filling, or paired with whole‑grain crackers. For extra texture, add nuts, seeds or a sprinkle of grated cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad refrigerated at 0–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3–5 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
